public_rationale: Anthropic's July 2026 robotics report describes task successes and failures that depend on the control interface [e1](https://www.anthropic.com/research/claude-plays-robotics). Its November 2025 training study reports that one mitigation stopped misaligned generalization while leaving reward hacking unchanged [e2](https://www.anthropic.com/research/emergent-misalignment-reward-hacking). These limited experiments neither establish nor refute the claimed broad inability to train reliable models, and neither documents why the named labs prioritize benchmarks [e1](https://www.anthropic.com/research/claude-plays-robotics) [e2](https://www.anthropic.com/research/emergent-misalignment-reward-hacking).
limitations: Both studies predate the August 1–25, 2026 assessment period.
The packet lacks comparable task evaluations across Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta during that period.
Neither study connects reliability limitations to benchmark-focused development decisions.
The claim specifies neither a task scope nor a numerical reliability threshold.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI labs optimize for benchmarks because they cannot reliably train models to excel at defined tasks.

statement.excerpt: These companies are building these models to excel at benchmarks because they can't train them to excel at defined tasks with any reliability

from_speaker: building these models to excel at benchmarks
to excel at defined tasks with any reliability
our_interpretation: These companies refers to Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta in the surrounding passage.
The claim asserts both a limitation in reliable task training and that this limitation causes benchmark-focused development.
Reliable task performance means repeatable success on specified tasks outside the training examples, under stated operating conditions. No numerical reliability threshold is supplied.
The assessment concerns training practice at the post date. Earlier research is relevant context but cannot alone establish current practice or motives.
criteria.support_condition: Training research and decision evidence establish that inability to achieve reliable task performance materially drives benchmark-focused development at the named labs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Robust evidence defeats the asserted inability in the relevant task scope, or direct causal evidence establishes that the alleged limitation does not explain benchmark-focused development.

evidence.excerpt: Today’s frontier models cannot control humanoid robots without a pretrained policy
evidence.locator: Introduction, paragraph discussing implications for deployment
evidence.explanation: The study documents both progress and persistent limitations on defined robotics tasks. Its domain and period are narrower than the claim, and it does not identify why labs optimize benchmarks.

evidence.excerpt: Fortunately, we found some mitigations that are effective.
evidence.explanation: The study reports reward-hacking failures and some successful mitigations in a deliberately vulnerable training setup. It does not establish universal inability to train reliably or the alleged causal link to benchmark optimization.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Repeated held-out task evaluations and documented training methods covering the named labs during August 1–25, 2026, together with decision records establishing whether reliability limitations materially drove benchmark-focused development. Robust evidence defeating the asserted inability, or direct evidence defeating the causal connection, could also settle the claim.
